The NFS Department aims to make some subtle yet timely changes to its Masters of Science (MS) in Nutrition program, based on feedback from students and alumni, as well as changing needs in the workforce.
The first is to change the somewhat vague 3-credit ³science´ requirement to NFS ª Epidemiology of Nutrition & Chronic Disease (3 credits).
The second is to add tracks, so students can develop skills in related areas that will better prepare them for interprofessional careers.

The 3-credit science requirement has been in place for decades.
Over the years, it has been inconsistent, and challenging to decide upon at an individual student level.
The recent addition of NFS 550 to the graduate curriculum has resulted in a course option that meets the needs of NFS graduate students.
It covers important concepts such as study design, appropriate data interpretation, and dissemination.
The course also includes hands-on learning with data analyses and understanding the nuances of big data.
With an emphasis on critical thinking, this course also exposes learners to a diverse array of scientific literature.
By including this course in the NFS graduate curriculum, it allows consistent and solid training of our MS students.

As with many other fields, nutrition has become increasingly multidisciplinary.
Thus, students should gain multidisciplinary learning during their graduate training.
The introduction of tracks within the NFS MS program would allow students to add focus in an area relevant to their career goals.In consultation withthe URl Graduate School,the tracks have been planned toinclude a minimum of six credits from a related discipline.These credits would be included within the minimum of 3o credits towards MS graduation requirements.

Summary description of proposed program (not to exceed 2 pages) Since its founding in the 1970’s, the mission of the Master of Public Administration (MPA) program at the University of Rhode Island is to instill public values, knowledge, and expertise to

2 prepare our graduates to solve problems related to governance, nonprofit management, and policy with integrity, professionalism, and excellence to improve our communities and society.
To train our students to meet the challenges of the 21st Century, the MPA program is embarking on a series of program revisions and a transition to a fully online program to meet the current and anticipated future needs from employers and various stakeholders across Rhode Island, the region, and nationally.
Although the MPA program will transition to a fully online, accelerated (7-week) format and replace its current blended, 14-week modality, the MPA program will retain many of its successful core features, including the requirement that MPA graduates earn 36 credits.
The accelerated online MPA program also incorporates new curricular innovations that will expand student recruitment and student flexibility.
Additionally, the programmatic and curricular revisions outlined in this proposal are critical for the program to become accredited by the Network of Schools of Public Policy, Affairs, and Administration (NASPAA) – a long-standing goal of the program – in the coming years.

One of the structural revisions and innovations of the online MPA program is the creation of three certificate programs that offer students with both core training in public administration and policy but also specializations mirroring the Public Management and Policy Analysis concentrations in the current program.
The three 12-credit graduate certificates in the online MPA program are: the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy, Public Management, and Policy Analysis.
Students in the online MPA program will need to complete the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy graduate certificate, at least one of the other two MPA graduate certificates, earn at least 36 credits, and complete the capstone course to complete their MPA degree.
The core certificate that forms the basis for the MPA online program is the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy.

Students completing this certificate program will have an opportunity to learn about the historical and theoretical foundations of public administration and policy (PSC 501), ethical decision-making strategies (PSC 504), diversity and inclusion in the public sector (PSC 502), and an elective course focused on developing core skills or experience for a career in government, non-profits, or policy.
All students who want to earn their MPA degree will be required to complete this graduate certificate.
In addition to the certificate in Public Administration and Policy, students choosing to graduate with an MPA degree can choose to complete either one or two additional MPA-offered certificates that form the basis of an added credential or specialization that will make graduates competitive in the job market.
The first is a certificate in Public Management.
The coursework required for this certificate will help students become competitive applicants for positions requiring financial and budgetary expertise (PSC 506 & PSC 507), leadership skills, knowledge of administrative law and procedure (PSC 573), and the management of agency personnel (PSC 503).

Currently, there is an acute need in many cities and towns for Finance Director positions, which can be a town or city’s highest paid municipal position.
Additionally, these are skills increasingly

3 sought by nonprofit organizations. By creating a certificate program, we hope to fulfill this workforce need in the state of Rhode Island and beyond by offering incumbent employees and new students the opportunity to develop a competency in Public Management. Our aim is to have incumbent workers trained so that they will have opportunities for advancement, and their advancement will, in turn, create entry-level opportunities for others pursuing a certificate in Public Management or our students completing the MPA program. The second of these optional certificates is the Policy Analysis certificate. The coursework required for this certificate will help students develop research and analytical capabilities (PSC 583 & PSC 510), evaluate public programs (PSC 505), and navigate the public policy process (PSC 524 & PSC 510). These skills will allow them to become effective at shaping public policy either within public agencies or as part of a broader policymaking process. Students pursuing this certificate will develop skills that will allow them to be policy advocates, policy researchers, and/or communication specialists. The underlying philosophy of the URI MPA online program is that its modular design will guide students along pathways that will allow them to align their graduate study with their career ambitions. MPA graduates will have earned no less than 36 credits while completing the program. All students completing the full 36-credit program will: • Complete the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy (12 credits);

4 • Complete either the Policy Analysis certificate (12 credits) and/or the Public Management certificate (12 credits); • Complete the remaining 12 elective credits if only one certificate program is chosen between the Policy Analysis certificate or the Public Management certificate. Graduates may choose to pursued a stackable certificate in another program to add alongside the two MPA certificates. Upon approval of the online MPA program, the Department of Political Science will develop an Advanced Bachelors-to-Master (ABM) program for undergraduates seeking to enter the MPA program by completing twelve credits during their senior year. The design of the MPA online program is not only aligned with NASPAA accreditation guidelines but also meets the growing workplace needs in Rhode Island, the region, and nationally.
To gauge the current and future hiring needs of employers in the public and nonprofit sectors, the MPA director, Dr.
Aaron Ley, conducted a series of meetings with key government and nonprofit stakeholders throughout the state over the last two years.
The meetings included the Rhode Island League of Cities and Towns, the Rhode Island City and Town Managers Association, and various other state agencies like the Rhode Island Secretary of State’s office, among others.

These meetings revealed the growing need of individuals with management and finance backgrounds because employees currently holding these positions are beginning to reach the age of retirement.
These discussions were confirmed through the Director’s own anecdotal experience in Bristol where the town’s finance director chose to take a position closer to home.
During that hiring process for the replacement, the town observed that very few people in its applicant pool were qualified to fill this position.
Nationally, municipal Finance Director positions are among some of the highest paid municipal employees.
In order to address this workforce need, and as part of our migration of the MPA program to an online format, we are proposing the development of a stackable Public Management Certificate that will allow our students to enter our program in order to develop skills relating to public budgeting and finance.

This will allow incumbent workers and entry-level workers to quickly earn a competency in public management by completing a suite of four courses to fulfill this certificate, while also giving them the option of remaining in the program to complete the MPA Online program by completing the other 24 credits.
We hope that the training of incumbent workers will create opportunities for their advancement, which will create entry-level opportunities for others pursuing a certificate in Public Management or our students completing the MPA program.
This stackable certificate can be used by MPA students desiring a special competency in the area of public management, or for students in other graduate programs wanting to use their remaining electives to gain public management skills.

By bringing the MPA program online and creating three additional credentials

11 in Public Management, Policy Analysis, and the Professional Certificate in Public Administration and Policy, our objective is to allow graduate students to learn the management, budgeting, financial, and analytical skills necessary to govern effectively and advance in public management, policy analysis, and governance-related positions in Rhode Island and beyond, which will advance URI’s core mission values of ethical leadership, engaged learning, and civic leadership.
